claim: Heterozygous mutation of TBX3 causes Ulnar-mammary syndrome (UMS).
source: Heterozygous mutation of TBX3 causes Ulnar-mammary syndrome (UMS), initially described as a constellation of congenital limb defects, apocrine and mammary gland hypoplasia, and genital abnormalities (Pallister et al., 1976).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pallister et al., 1976

claim: Heart and conduction system defects have been described in mice and humans with abnormal Tbx3/TBX3 function.
source: Recently, heart and conduction system defects have also been described in mice and humans with abnormal Tbx3 (mice) and TBX3 (humans) function (Bakker et al., 2008; Frank et al., 2012; Linden et al., 2009; Meneghini et al., 2006; Mesbah et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Germline deletion of Tbx3 in mice results in embryonic lethality with heart, limb, and mammary defects.
source: Germline deletion of Tbx3 in mice results in embryonic lethality with heart, limb, and mammary defects (Davenport et al., 2003; Frank et al., 2012; 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 regulates pluripotency and cell fate in early development.
source: Tbx3 also regulates pluripotency and cell fate in early development (Cheng et al., 2012; Han et al., 2010; Kartikasari et al., 2013; Niwa et al., 2009; Weidgang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: TBX3 transcriptional repression controls expression of cell proliferation and senescence factors.
source: TBX3 transcriptional repression controls expression of cell proliferation and senescence factors (Brummelkamp et al., 2002; Kumar et al., 2014a)
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Abnormal TBX3 expression occurs in multiple cancers.
source: abnormal TBX3 expression occurs in multiple cancers (Liu et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2010; Peres and Prince, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: TBX3 regulates splicing and RNA metabolism.
source: TBX3 also regulates splicing and RNA metabolism (Kumar et al., 2014b).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: UMS limb phenotypes range in severity from hypoplasia of digit 5 to complete absence of forearm and hand.
source: UMS limb phenotypes are variable ranging in severity from hypoplasia of digit 5 to complete absence of forearm and hand (OMIM #181450).
evidence: Supported by citation to OMIM database

claim: Mouse Tbx3tm1Pa/tm1Pa mutant forelimbs lack posterior digits and the ulna.
source: Mouse Tbx3tm1Pa/tm1Pa (Davenport et al., 2003) and Tbx3Δfl/Δfl (Frank et al., 2013) mutant forelimbs lack posterior digits and the ulna.
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Hindlimbs of Tbx3tm1Pa/tm1Pa and Tbx3Δfl/Δfl null mutants have only a single digit.
source: Hindlimbs of Tbx3tm1Pa/tm1Pa and Tbx3Δfl/Δfl null mutants have only a single digit, but Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants also have pelvic defects (Frank et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Shh signaling in posterior mesenchyme promotes digit development.
source: Shh signaling in posterior mesenchyme promotes digit development and prevents processing of full length Gli3 (Gli3FL) to its repressor form, Gli3R, which constrains digit number (Litingtung et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: The balance of Gli transcriptional activation and repression is critical for proper digit number and patterning.
source: The balance of Gli transcriptional activation and repression is critical for proper digit number and patterning (Cao et al., 2013; Hill et al., 2007; Litingtung et al., 2002; te Welscher et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2000; 2007a; Zhulyn et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: In mammals, the limited, partial proteolytic processing of Gli3FL to Gli3R requires functional primary cilia.
source: In mammals, the limited, partial proteolytic processing of Gli3FL to Gli3R requires functional primary cilia, the ciliary protein Kif7 (Goetz and Anderson, 2010; Liu et al., 2005), as well as balanced activity of Sufu and the ubiquitin ligase adaptors βTrCP and Spop (Chen et al., 2009; Wang and Li, 2006; Wang et al., 2010; Wen et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 is expressed in discrete anterior and posterior mesenchymal domains in the limb buds from embryonic day (E) 9.5.
source: Tbx3 is expressed in discrete anterior and posterior mesenchymal domains in the limb buds from embryonic day (E) 9.5 (Figure 1A,C,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Prx1Cre initiates Cre activity at ~14-somite stage (ss) in the forelimb-forming region of the lateral plate mesoderm (LPM).
source: This driver initiates Cre activity at ~14-somite stage (ss) in the forelimb-forming region of the lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) (Hasson et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Complete ablation of Tbx3 mRNA and protein in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb mesenchyme occurs by E9.5.
source: In situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry confirm complete ablation of Tbx3 mRNA and protein in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb mesenchyme by E9.5 (Figure 1B–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures using in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry

claim: Tbx3 expression in the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) is preserved in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Expression in the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) is preserved (Figure 1B,D,F).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3;PrxCre mutants survive to adulthood with forelimb defects.
source: Unlike mid-gestational lethality seen in constitutive Tbx3 mutants (Davenport et al., 2003; Frank et al., 2013), Tbx3;PrxCre mutants survive to adulthood with forelimb defects (Video 1)
evidence: Supported by comparison to published studies and data shown in video

claim: 100% of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants have bilateral preaxial polysyndactyly of digit 1.
source: 100% have bilateral preaxial polysyndactyly of digit 1 (called PPD1 in humans [Materna-Kiryluk et al., 2013]), and 70% lack digit 5 (Figure 1G–J).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures and citation

claim: 70% of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants lack digit 5.
source: 100% have bilateral preaxial polysyndactyly of digit 1 (called PPD1 in humans [Materna-Kiryluk et al., 2013]), and 70% lack digit 5 (Figure 1G–J).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Loss of digit 5 was bilateral in 6/18 Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Loss of digit 5 was bilateral in 6/18 and in the remaining, only affected the left forelimb (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in table

claim: In 12/18 Tbx3;PrxCre mutants, loss of digit 5 only affected the left forelimb.
source: Loss of digit 5 was bilateral in 6/18 and in the remaining, only affected the left forelimb (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in table

claim: Asymmetric loss of digit 5 in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants is not due to asymmetric activity of PrxCre.
source: This is not due to asymmetric activity of PrxCre because it is also observed in Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants (Δfl = recombined floxed conditional allele) where no Cre activity is involved (Frank et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study and inference from comparison

claim: Delayed ossification of the humerus is observed in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Delayed ossification of the humerus (Figure 1H) and loss of the deltoid tuberosity (Figure 1J) were also observed.
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Loss of the deltoid tuberosity is observed in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Delayed ossification of the humerus (Figure 1H) and loss of the deltoid tuberosity (Figure 1J) were also observed.
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Abnormal limb bud morphology is evident by E10.5 in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Abnormal limb bud morphology is evident by E10.5 (Figure 1L) and evolving skeletal defects at E11.5 by the altered pattern of Sox9 expression (Figure 1N).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Evolving skeletal defects are evident at E11.5 in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants by altered pattern of Sox9 expression.
source: Abnormal limb bud morphology is evident by E10.5 (Figure 1L) and evolving skeletal defects at E11.5 by the altered pattern of Sox9 expression (Figure 1N).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Germline Tbx3 null mutants (genotype Tbx3Δfl/Δfl) have more severe forelimb defects than Tbx3;PrxCre conditional mutants.
source: Germline Tbx3 null mutants (genotype Tbx3Δfl/Δfl) have more severe forelimb defects than Tbx3;PrxCre conditional mutants: of the few Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants that survive to E13.5, 100% have agenesis of the ulna and digits 3–5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: 100% of Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants that survive to E13.5 have agenesis of the ulna and digits 3–5.
source: Germline Tbx3 null mutants (genotype Tbx3Δfl/Δfl) have more severe forelimb defects than Tbx3;PrxCre conditional mutants: of the few Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants that survive to E13.5, 100% have agenesis of the ulna and digits 3–5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutant hindlimbs have a single digit and no fibula.
source: Their hindlimbs have a single digit and no fibula (Frank et al., 2013), phenocopying Shh and Hand2 null mutants (Galli et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutant hindlimb phenotype phenocopies Shh and Hand2 null mutants.
source: Their hindlimbs have a single digit and no fibula (Frank et al., 2013), phenocopying Shh and Hand2 null mutants (Galli et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3fl/fl;Fgf8mcm/mcm mutants have normal limbs.
source: Tbx3fl/fl;Fgf8mcm/mcm mutants have normal limbs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2L)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: Phenotypes of Tbx3fl/fl;PrxCre and Tbx3fl/fl;RarbCre are indistinguishable.
source: phenotypes of Tbx3fl/fl;PrxCre and Tbx3fl/fl;RarbCre are indistinguishable (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D versus N).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: The severe phenotypes of Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants are not due to a required function of Tbx3 in the AER.
source: The results with both Cre drivers indicate that the severe phenotypes of Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants are not due to a required function of Tbx3 in the AER.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results with two different Cre drivers

claim: Limb initiation in the LPM requires Tbx5 expression in the prospective forelimb territory as early as the 8ss.
source: Limb initiation in the LPM requires Tbx5 expression in the prospective forelimb territory as early as the 8ss (Minguillon et al., 2005), upstream of Hand2 (Agarwal et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 is expressed in the LPM from E7.5.
source: Tbx3 is expressed in the LPM from E7.5 (Figure 2A–C').
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3-expressing progenitors in the LPM at E8-8.5 give rise to most E10 forelimb mesenchyme.
source: Lineage tracing with a novel Tbx3mcm allele (Thomas et al., in preparation) revealed that Tbx3-expressing progenitors in the LPM at E8-8.5 give rise to most E10 forelimb mesenchyme in Tbx3mcm/+;RosaLacZ/+ embryos (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure using lineage tracing

claim: Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants have decreased LPM expression of Tbx5.
source: Consistent with a role for Tbx3 in limb initiation, Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants have decreased LPM expression of Tbx5 (Figure 2E,F)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants have visible defects in forelimb initiation and early limb bud morphology.
source: visible defects in forelimb initiation and early limb bud morphology (Figure 2G,H)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3Δfl/Δfl mutants have disrupted expression of Hand2.
source: and disrupted expression of Hand2 (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Early stage Tbx5 expression and limb bud initiation are unaffected in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: In contrast, early stage Tbx5 expression and limb bud initiation are unaffected in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,B')
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: Most Tbx3;PrxCre mutants lack digit 5.
source: Most Tbx3;PrxCre mutants lack digit 5, whose specification and formation depend on 'early phase' Shh signaling beginning at E9.5 (Harfe et al., 2004; Scherz et al., 2007; Zhu and Mackem, 2011; Zhu et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Digit 5 specification and formation depend on 'early phase' Shh signaling beginning at E9.5.
source: Most Tbx3;PrxCre mutants lack digit 5, whose specification and formation depend on 'early phase' Shh signaling beginning at E9.5 (Harfe et al., 2004; Scherz et al., 2007; Zhu and Mackem, 2011; Zhu et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Hand2 protein is required to activate Shh expression in the limb bud.
source: Hand2 protein is required to activate Shh expression in the limb bud (Benazet and Zeller, 2009; Galli et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Hand2 transcripts are reduced in E9.5 and E10.5 Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb buds.
source: We found that Hand2 transcripts are reduced in E9.5 and E10.5 Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb buds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D,D'; Figure 3A, A',F)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Shh expression is reduced in E9.5 and E10.5 Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb buds.
source: as is Shh expression (Figure 3B,B',F; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Expression of Ptch1 and Grem1 is markedly reduced in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant forelimb buds.
source: Expression of two targets and effectors of Shh signaling, Ptch1 and Grem1, is also markedly reduced (Figure 3C',E'; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3 expression in posterior limb mesoderm begins earlier than in the anterior compartment.
source: Tbx3 expression in posterior limb mesoderm begins earlier than in the anterior compartment (Figure 1A,C)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3 is required for normal Hand2 in posterior mesoderm.
source: and is required for normal Hand2 in posterior mesoderm (Figure 3A, Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D') (Rallis et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures and citation

claim: Post-initiation, Tbx3 functions downstream of Tbx5 and upstream of Hand2.
source: Thus, intact Tbx5 expression in Tbx3;PrxCre E9.5 forelimbs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B') indicates that post-initiation, Tbx3 functions downstream of Tbx5 and upstream of Hand2.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing intact Tbx5 expression

claim: Shh and other hedgehog pathway members and target genes were present among the significantly dysregulated transcripts in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant limb buds.
source: Shh and other hedgehog pathway members and target genes (Lettice et al., 2003; Probst et al., 2011; Vokes et al., 2008; McGlinn et al., 2005)(Lewandowski et al., 2015) were present among the significantly dysregulated transcripts (Supplementary file 1)
evidence: Supported by microarray data in supplementary file and citations

claim: Decreased levels of Shh-activated transcripts (Gli1, Hand2, Osr1, Dkk1, Tbx2, Cntfr, Pkdcc) were detected in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant limb buds.
source: In addition to decreased levels of Shh- activated transcripts (Gli1, Hand2, Osr1, Dkk1, Tbx2, Cntfr, Pkdcc), we noted increased Rprm, Zic3, Hand1, and Gli3 transcripts and confirmed these with qPCR and in situ hybridization at E10.5–11 (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Increased Rprm, Zic3, Hand1, and Gli3 transcripts were detected in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant limb buds.
source: In addition to decreased levels of Shh- activated transcripts (Gli1, Hand2, Osr1, Dkk1, Tbx2, Cntfr, Pkdcc), we noted increased Rprm, Zic3, Hand1, and Gli3 transcripts and confirmed these with qPCR and in situ hybridization at E10.5–11 (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures using qPCR and in situ hybridization

claim: At E10.5, there was a statistically significant decrease in the fraction of proliferating cells in the posterior mesenchyme of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Assay of cell proliferation in E10.5 and E11.5 limb buds using anti-phosphohistone H3 immunohistochemistry revealed that at E10.5 there was a statistically significant decrease in the fraction of proliferating cells in the posterior mesenchyme (Figure 3K–M).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures using immunohistochemistry

claim: At E11.5, proliferation was significantly decreased in both the anterior and posterior mesenchyme of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: At E11.5, proliferation was significantly decreased in both the anterior and posterior mesenchyme, indicating a global reduction in the number of mitotic cells in mutants (Figure 3N–P).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: 5th digit agenesis is attributable, at least in part, to decreased cell number.
source: This suggests that 5th digit agenesis is attributable, at least in part, to decreased cell number, as opposed to decreased proliferation specifically in digit 5 progenitors.
evidence: Inferred from proliferation data

claim: Normal levels of anterior AER cell death were observed at E10.5 in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Assay for apoptosis using TUNEL showed normal levels of anterior AER cell death at E10.5, as we have previously reported in this region (Moon and Capecchi, 2000) (Figure 3K,L).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures using TUNEL assay and citation

claim: Proliferation of limb mesenchyme depends on activity of FGF8 and FGF4 from the AER.
source: Proliferation of limb mesenchyme depends on activity of FGF8 and FGF4 from the AER (Boulet et al., 2004; Moon and Capecchi, 2000; Sun et al., 2002)
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Integrity of the AER requires Shh activity in posterior mesenchyme.
source: and integrity of this structure requires Shh activity in posterior mesenchyme (Chiang et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Fgf4 transcripts were increased in posterior mesenchyme while decreased in anterior in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Despite decreased Shh expression in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants, Fgf4 transcripts were increased in posterior mesenchyme while decreased in anterior (detected by RNA-Seq, Supplementary files 3,4 and qPCR, Figure 3—figure supplement 4)
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq and qPCR data

claim: qPCR detected increased Fgf8 expression in the posterior AER of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: qPCR detected increased Fgf8 expression in the posterior AER (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in figure supplement

claim: There was no evidence of altered downstream FGF signaling in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants as expression of Etv4, Etv5, Dusp6 and Sprys was unchanged.
source: Despite these changes in transcript levels, there was no evidence of altered downstream FGF signaling as expression of Etv4, Etv5, Dusp6 and Sprys was unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 5, note these transcripts are not listed in Supplementary files 3 or 4 because they did not meet criteria for differential expression).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: The level of Shh pathway activity in posterior mesenchyme of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants is sufficient to maintain ectodermal FGF signaling.
source: We conclude that despite the decrement in Shh pathway activity in posterior mesenchyme of Tbx3;PrxCre mutants, the level is sufficient to maintain ectodermal FGF signaling, consistent with preserved limb outgrowth.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data on FGF signaling

claim: RNA-Seq analysis showed no evidence of ectopic hedgehog activity in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant anterior compartments.
source: RNA-Seq analysis of control versus mutant anterior compartments (Supplementary file 4) showed no evidence of ectopic hedgehog activity in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants, and this was confirmed by in situ hybridization and qPCR for Shh and Ptch1 (Figure 3B–C', Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq, in situ hybridization, and qPCR data

claim: Gli3 transcripts were increased in mutant limb buds.
source: Although Gli3 transcripts were increased in mutant limb buds (Figure 3D',F; Supplementary file 1)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures and supplementary file

claim: Targets of Gli3R transcriptional repression such as Zic3, Epha3, Hoxd13 were overexpressed in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: targets of Gli3R transcriptional repression such as Zic3, Epha3, Hoxd13 (McGlinn et al., 2005; Vokes et al., 2008) were overexpressed when assayed by microarray, RNA-Seq, qPCR and in situ hybridization (Figure 3 G-J, Supplementary files 1,3,4).
evidence: Supported by multiple methods of gene expression analysis and citations

claim: Gli3R protein was markedly decreased in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant anterior mesenchyme.
source: Gli3R protein was markedly decreased (7.4 fold on this representative immunoblot) with multiple bands of lower molecular weight than Gli3R present specifically in Tbx3;PrxCre mutant anterior mesenchyme (mutant anterior compartment: MA, Figure 4A, red box).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in figure

claim: Gli3FL was virtually undetectable in mutant anterior mesenchyme.
source: Gli3FL was virtually undetectable in mutant anterior mesenchyme (Figure 4A').
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in figure

claim: Tbx3 is required for stability of Gli3FL and Gli3R proteins in the anterior limb mesenchyme.
source: These findings indicate that Tbx3 is required for stability of Gli3FL and Gli3R proteins in the anterior limb mesenchyme, and are consistent with the PPD phenotype observed here and in other models of Gli3R deficiency (Hill et al., 2009; Naruse et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2007a).
evidence: Inferred from experimental data and supported by citations

claim: Kif7 was among the Tbx3 interacting proteins identified by mass spectrometry.
source: In an independent experiment to identify Tbx3 interacting partners, we performed Tbx3 co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) on E10.5 mouse embryo lysates, followed by mass spectrometry (Kumar et al., 2014b). Surprisingly, Kif7 was among the Tbx3 interacting proteins identified.
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data and citation

claim: Kif7 is a ciliary protein that modulates activity of the Hedgehog pathway.
source: Kif7 is a ciliary protein that modulates activity of the Hedgehog pathway (Hui and Angers, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Kif7 is required for proper formation of a 'cilium tip' compartment that regulates Gli function.
source: It is required for proper formation of a 'cilium tip' compartment that regulates Gli function (He et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Kif7 is required for the regulated, partial proteolytic processing of GliFL to Gli3R.
source: and for the regulated, partial proteolytic processing of GliFL to Gli3R (Chen et al., 2009; Cheung et al., 2009; Endoh-Yamagami et al., 2009; Law et al., 2012; Ryan and Chiang, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Human and mouse Kif7 mutants have PPD.
source: As in Tbx3;PrxCre and Gli3+/- mutants (Hill et al., 2009), human and mouse Kif7 mutants have PPD (Cheung et al. 2009; Endoh-Yamagami et al. 2009; Putoux et al. 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 co-immunoprecipitates with Kif7 in developing limb.
source: Immunoprecipitation of protein lysates from E10.5 forelimb buds showed that Tbx3 co-immunoprecipitates (co-IPs) with Kif7, confirming interaction of Kif7 and Tbx3 in the developing limb (Figure 4B; specificity and efficiency of Kif7 IP in this experiment is shown in Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by co-IP data shown in figures

claim: Tbx3 and Kif7 directly interact.
source: We next tested whether these proteins directly interact by overexpressing Flag-tagged Kif7 and Myc-tagged Tbx3 in HEK293 cells and immunoprecipitating for either Flag or Myc, followed by immunoblotting for Tbx3 (Figure 4D) or Kif7 (Figure 4E). Both experiments confirmed direct interaction of the tagged proteins.
evidence: Supported by co-IP data from overexpression experiments shown in figures

claim: In 16% of control cilia, Kif7 was detected in two punctae or as a streak along the cilia.
source: In 16% of control cilia, Kif7 was detected in two punctae (presumed base and tip) or as a streak along the cilia, but this was only the case in 6% of mutant cilia (Figure 4H, p<0.001).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure

claim: In 6% of Tbx3;PrxCre mutant cilia, Kif7 was detected in two punctae or as a streak along the cilia.
source: In 16% of control cilia, Kif7 was detected in two punctae (presumed base and tip) or as a streak along the cilia, but this was only the case in 6% of mutant cilia (Figure 4H, p<0.001).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure

claim: There was no significant difference in the number of Kif7+ cilia between controls and mutants.
source: There was no significant difference in the number of Kif7+ cilia rather, there were more single puncta cilia in mutants than controls (Figure 4H, 84% vs 71%, p<0.001).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure

claim: There were more single puncta cilia in mutants than controls (84% vs 71%).
source: There was no significant difference in the number of Kif7+ cilia rather, there were more single puncta cilia in mutants than controls (Figure 4H, 84% vs 71%, p<0.001).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure

claim: No difference in the amount of Kif7 protein was detected in control versus mutant limb bud compartments by western blot.
source: We did not detect any difference in the amount of Kif7 protein in control versus mutant limb bud compartments by western blot (Figure 4I, representative of four4 separate experiments).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in figure

claim: Levels of Kif7 mRNA in the anterior limb mesenchyme were unaffected by loss of Tbx3.
source: Levels of Kif7 mRNA in the anterior limb mesenchyme were unaffected by loss of Tbx3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: One feature of Kif7-/- mutants is excess Sufu due to increased protein stability.
source: One feature of Kif7-/-mutants is excess Sufu due to increased protein stability (Hsu et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study

claim: Transcript levels of Sufu were unchanged in mutant forelimbs.
source: Transcript levels of Sufu were unchanged in mutant forelimbs (Figure 3—figure supplement 4, no difference was detected by microarray or RNA-Seq).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: Increased amounts of Sufu and Spop protein were present in mutant limb buds.
source: However, increased amounts of Sufu (and Spop) protein were present in mutant limb buds (Figure 4J,K; increased 1.5 fold in both cases).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in figures

claim: Humans and mice with Kif7 mutations have abnormally long cilia because Kif7 reduces the rate of microtubule growth in the ciliary axoneme.
source: Humans and mice with Kif7 mutations have abnormally long cilia because Kif7 reduces the rate of microtubule growth in the ciliary axoneme (He et al., 2014; Putoux et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3;PrxCre mutants have an increased fraction of larger cilia and an average volume 18% greater than controls.
source: Consistent with aberrant, but not absent, Kif7 function, we found that while the range of cilia volumes detected were the same between mutants and controls, the distribution was not: mutants have an increased fraction of larger cilia and an average volume 18% greater (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B; 475 and 575 cilia assayed in controls and mutants, respectively).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure supplement

claim: The derived length of cilia was 6% greater in Tbx3;PrxCre mutants.
source: Mutants and controls had superimposable surface area/volume ratios (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), indicating that the shape of cilia was not different thus, the derived length was 6% greater in mutants.
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in figure supplement

claim: Loss of Tbx3 results in aberrant ciliary localization of Kif7.
source: Together, these findings indicate that loss of Tbx3 results in aberrant ciliary localization of Kif7 and are consistent with abnormal Kif7 function.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data on Kif7 localization and cilia morphology

claim: Kif7 and other proteins required for Gli3 processing and function are present in, or translocate to, primary cilia in response to Hedgehog pathway activity.
source: Kif7 and other proteins required for Gli3 processing and function are present in, or translocate to, primary cilia in response to Hedgehog pathway activity (Goetz and Anderson, 2010; Ryan and Chiang, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 is present in control limb anterior mesenchymal cilia.
source: Dual immunostaining for Tbx3 and Arl13b on whole mount optically sectioned E10.5 forelimbs shows that Tbx3 is present in control limb anterior mesenchymal cilia (Figure 5 A-E, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in figures

claim: Specificity of Tbx3 staining was confirmed by loss of signal in mesenchymal cilia of Tbx3;PrxCre mutant limbs.
source: Specificity of Tbx3 staining was confirmed by loss of signal in mesenchymal cilia of Tbx3;PrxCre mutant limbs (Figure 5F-J, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in figures

claim: 18/50 anterior mesenchymal cilia (36%) were Tbx3+ in controls.

claim: Tbx3 is present at baseline in cilia, and is trafficked to cilia in response to hedgehog signaling.

claim: Gli3FL stability and partial processing versus complete degradation are regulated by opposing actions of Sufu and Spop.

evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: In the absence of Smoothened activation, mammalian Sufu recruits GSK3β to phosphorylate Gli3FL downstream of PKA, allowing for its partial processing to Gli3R.
source: In the absence of Smoothened activation, mammalian Sufu recruits GSK3β to phosphorylate Gli3FL downstream of PKA, allowing for its partial processing to Gli3R (which requires Kif7 and intact cilia) (Kise et al., 2009; Tempe et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Spop is an adaptor for Cullin3-based E3 ubiquitin ligase that drives complete degradation of Gli3FL in the absence of Sufu.
source: Spop is an adaptor for Cullin3-based E3 ubiquitin ligase that drives complete degradation of Gli3FL in the absence of Sufu, but facilitates its processing to Gli3R when Sufu is present (Humke et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Tbx3 does not interact with Sufu or Spop.

claim: Gli3FL is virtually undetectable in Tbx3;PrxCre anterior mesenchyme.

evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in figures

claim: Despite increased amount of Sufu, it fails to prevent degradation of Gli3FL in the absence of Tbx3.

claim: Normal stoichiometry of the interaction of Gli3 proteins with Sufu requires Tbx3.

However, there was a robust and reproducible interaction in mutants despite the decrease in the total amount of Gli3 proteins.
